summary: Module 5 VERIFY answers. (1) Severity assigned: the active auth bypass with cross-user data exposure is SEV1 -- active security exploitation with data exposure and regulatory implications; the thing that would demote it to SEV2 is a narrowed blast radius (e.g., the data exposed is non-sensitive, or the vulnerability requires an already-authenticated trusted session, so no cross-tenant leak) or proof it is not being actively exploited; conversely SEV2 becomes SEV1 when exploitation is live and data is leaving. (2) First stakeholder update (non-technical VP, demo question): 'Incident update 09:41 UTC (SEV1) -- Users are able to see a small set of other users' private information, and we have taken the affected area under investigation. Our demo uses only test accounts and is not affected by the exposed data path. What we know: which area is involved, that the API remains up, that the data is a limited set. What we do not know yet: how many users and for how long. Next action: reproduce the exposure in a sandbox now. Next update: 09:56 UTC or sooner if we find the root cause. If you want the demo to go ahead, use the seeded test account and nothing else.' -- A non-technical VP understands 'users can see other users' private data', the demo answer is explicit, and the next-update expectation is set. (3) Pressure to say 'it is fine': yes, real pressure, but giving in costs: the VP tells the prospect 'our security is solid', next week the breach becomes public, the VP looks like a liar, the prospect walks, trust evaporates, and the engineer owns an avoidable lie on top of a real incident. The truthful line: 'I cannot confirm or deny a breach yet; I can tell you we have isolated the exposed path, and I will have a definitive answer by 09:56.' (4) Alert-to-first-update gap: target <= 5 minutes, structurally enforced by writing the update first from a template (severity, knowns, unknowns, next action, ETA); an under-2-minute update is usually a panicked 'looking into it', which is why the template forces the five fields so even a fast update is useful, not filler.
evidence: First stakeholder update drafted with severity, demo answer, knowns, unknowns, next action, ETA
Honest answer to the VP-pressure question with played-forward cost
Alert-to-update gap target <= 5 minutes via template
